newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - June 10.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:
* Federal judges in Texas and New York have shut down some World Wide Web sites, at the behest of the recording industry, for illegally distributing sound recordings over the Internet.
* Microsoft Corp has invested $1 billion in Comcast Corp, a move that sent cable stocks soaring.
* Nicolas Cage's "Con Air" posted 11 top-spot bows at the overseas box office over the weekend, bringing in $5 million.

* Universal TV Group Chairman Gregory Meidel is in serious talks with DreamWorks' syndication co-chief Ken Solomon about taking the post of Universal TV president, which Tom Thayer announced last week he'd be vacating.
* Jujamcyn Theaters and Pace Theatrical Group are teaming up to offer an old-style Hollywood studio system that oversees projects from conception to a birth on Broadway and beyond.
* News Corp Ltd's Fox Sports West 2 is using the planned acquisition of the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team to sign up cable operators.
* After the handover of Hong Kong to the Chinese July 1, the picture business is hoping to enjoy a more thriving community.
